text: Earlier that summer afternoon, the two had walked together in the fields, and when they sat down on a grassy bank, Wing spoke with a sudden, eager passion. <break time="0.8s" /> You are destroying yourself, he cried, because you are too much influenced by the people in this town, and you are afraid of your own dreams. <break time="0.8s" /> You must try to forget all you have learned, Wing said, and from now on you must shut your ears to the roaring voices around you. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, with his voice growing soft, he painted a picture of a golden age in which young men came across the green countryside, some on foot and some on horses. <break time="0.8s" /> They gathered at the feet of an old man who sat beneath a tree in a tiny garden, and they listened eagerly to his words. <break time="0.8s" /> As he talked, Wing forgot his hands, and slowly they crept forward and came to rest on George Willards shoulders. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a look of horror swept over his face, and jumping to his feet, he thrust his hands deep into his pockets while tears came into his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> I must go home now, and I cannot talk with you any longer, he said nervously, and he hurried away across the meadow without looking back, leaving the young man puzzled and afraid.
